answer: HYPOTHESIS: Urban land use promoted the invasion of non-native plants in the Barcelona region, but its effect depended strongly on the type (introduction pathway) of the introduced plants. In plots with more urban cover (50 m buffer, 2009), the probability of harbouring unintentionally introduced (weedy/ruderal) non-native plants was significantly higher (log-odds +1.18; cluster-bootstrap 95% CI +0.21 to +2.25), the probability of harbouring gardening-origin plants was unchanged (log-odds −0.13; CI −1.20 to +1.04), and the probability of harbouring agriculture/forestry-origin plants was significantly lower (log-odds −1.72; CI −2.61 to −0.79). In count models, mean invasion richness increased with urban cover for unintentional (total log-rate slope ≈ +1.08) and gardening (≈ +0.72) species but decreased for agriculture/forestry species (≈ −0.57), and this pathway ranking was consistent at the 50 m, 500 m and 1000 m landscape scales. The plants that actually invaded urbanized lowland plots were spatially widespread generalists: unintentionally introduced species occupied more plots (mean 9.6 vs 3.9 gardening, 2.3 agri-forest), more habitat types (2.8 vs 2.0 vs 1.6) and larger areas of occupancy (6.2 vs 2.8 vs 2.2 10-km cells), and annual growth forms were the most successful invaders (AOO 6.7 vs 3.2 vs 2.3). In short, urbanization acted as a filter favouring weedy, unintentionally introduced, habitat-generalist species over the ornamental (gardening) and crop/forest species that make up the bulk of the region's introduction pool (75% of 1985–2019 introductions were gardening-origin).

payload.workflow: 1) Data audit of all four files (row counts, schema match, NAs, duplicated multi-pathway species, tip-label alignment, collinearity VIFs). 2) Reshaped invaded_niche_pathways.csv to long form (632 plots x 3 pathways = 1896 rows; response = current per-plot count per pathway). 3) Primary model: Poisson GLM via IRLS (glm_fit.py, since statsmodels GLM was unavailable in the runtime) with count ~ pathway * urban.2009.50m + Δurban.1956_2009 + progressive.1956.2009.50m + cropland.2009.50m + habitat + elevation + distance.road + distance.stream + longitude + latitude, cluster-robust sandwich covariance grouped by plot (the (1|plot) analogue for the three pathway rows per plot); annual.temperature/rainfall dropped for collinearity with elevation (r = -0.96/0.86). 4) Zero-inflation diagnostics (observed vs fitted zeros) and two-part model (binomial presence + Poisson richness, both cluster-robust). 5) Cluster bootstrap (B=199, resampling plots) for the key terms and for the presence model, after detecting strong residual spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I = 3.4, p = 0.01; linear lon/lat controls added). 6) Sensitivity refits at 500 m and 1000 m urban exposures. 7) Species-level permutation ANOVAs (999 permutations) of invasion success (log plots, niche breadth, habitat range, AOO) by pathway (81 species x pathway rows), growth form, dispersal, vegetative (77 deduplicated species); PVP phylogenetic-signal test on the 81-tip tree (supplementary). 8) Contingency table chi2 + gardening-share trend as regional context. All outputs written to analysis_results.md; script re-runs end-to-end in ~26 s (exit 0).
